cases.visibleGeometry: An irregular cluster of high, angular ridges and blocks occupies the northwest quarter; a curved track passes its east side. A smaller isolated rise lies farther south. Similar rough outcrops occur across the surrounding terrain. The aerial view shows exposed grey rock, scattered shrubs and the track.
cases.alternatives: Natural bedrock outcrop and loose stone are the strongest explanation. The southern rise may be another rock exposure. Some apparent straight segments could be chance joints or low walls; the nearby route is modern access.
cases.supportLimits: The main rough cluster contains many interpolated cells. Its exact relief and apparent internal edges need original return checks. Aerial detail does not establish construction or age.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth slope meets a rougher, tree-covered surface along a curving east-west break near the patch middle. Several small knolls and angular rough spots lie on both sides. The aerial view places a dirt route along the break; rough areas coincide with trees and exposed stone.
cases.alternatives: The break is plausibly a route cut or field edge following natural relief. Rough spots may be bedrock, vegetation effects or erosion. No coherent enclosed or platform-like form stands apart from these patterns.
cases.supportLimits: Scattered interpolated cells coincide with trees and the rough break. Fine shape and small protrusions cannot be trusted without source returns. Aerial imagery shows current surface cover only.

cases.visibleGeometry: Regular, closely spaced cultivation ridges fill much of the west and south. Straight field boundaries meet a curving east-west track near the centre. A small narrow protrusion at that junction aligns with a tree or hedge in the aerial view. The northeast field is rougher with scattered trees.
cases.alternatives: The lines and ridges match agricultural plots, ploughing and access routes. The junction protrusion may be a tree base, boundary stone or drainage/track feature. No distinct older enclosure or mound is apparent.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation is concentrated along hedges, tracks and trees, including the junction. Their small relief forms need source returns to distinguish ground from canopy or smoothing effects.

cases.visibleGeometry: Two gently curving, nearly parallel field boundaries run across the patch, enclosing an area with scattered tree-related roughness. Fine cultivation ridges fill the ground above and below. A small raised angular spot near the north boundary corresponds to exposed rock in the aerial view; the lower boundary follows a dirt route.
cases.alternatives: Agricultural boundaries, cultivation and access paths explain the dominant lines. The isolated rise appears to be rock. Tree cover and occasional stones account for the irregular relief between boundaries.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolated cells cluster on both boundaries and around tree positions. The slight field roughness is sensitive to ground-return gaps; neither image set establishes construction or age.
